text: #To the auntie in the injection room: Please don’t criticize patients about their clothing. It’s the patient’s right. The doctor hasn’t been bothered at all. The doctor is lovely and takes very good care of them. I’ve been going here since I was 17 and now I’m 25. But the nurses always have sour faces. Especially the nurse in the injection room. Today, I just went and got criticized by her about my attire. I was dressed comfortably and neatly today. The doctor had to inject my shoulder and arm. But she asked me how I was going to take off my clothes. I asked her where I was going to get the injection. I told her my shoulder. I told her I didn’t think I’d get the injection. Then the auntie said, “Come to the doctor and dress comfortably. That’s the most comfortable way.” For the shoulder injection, just pull down your shirt. The arm won’t be a problem because you took off your coat. I don’t like the auntie’s criticism of my clothing. At first, I thought she was going to inject herself and that’s why there was a problem. The doctor did the injecting herself like every time. The doctor didn’t say anything. I didn’t respond. She told me to come to the doctor and dress comfortably. I don’t understand how the auntie’s normal way is. Everything else is fine. Except for the auntie in the injection room, if possible, don't talk to the patients. They'll get mentally ill.
